title: Cisco ISE Logs through Splunk Edge Processor — Pipeline Health and Routing
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Cisco ISE Logs through Splunk Edge Processor — Pipeline Health and Routing' only. Does not replace full NAC policy design or firewall rule authoring or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `network_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `network_cisco_ise_logs_through_splunk_edge_processor_pip` (UC-17.1.59), SOC dashboard panel "Network — Cisco ISE Logs through Splunk Edge Processor — Pipeline Health and Routing", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:network_controls.

compliance.assurance_rationale: Art.21(2)(g) effectiveness measurement — pipeline-health is one input.
AU-4 (Audit Log Storage Capacity) — pipeline drops impact log fidelity.
compliance.controlObjective: Audit-log fidelity preservation when normalizing data through Edge Processor.
Logging-pipeline fidelity demonstrated end-to-end through the edge layer.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=_internal` sourcetype='ep:metrics' that satisfy the UC-17.1.59 SPL filters for 'Cisco ISE Logs through Splunk Edge Processor — Pipeline Health and Routing'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `_internal` / `ep:metrics` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `network_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-17.1.59.

dataSources: Splunk Edge Processor / Ingest Processor metrics from `index=_internal sourcetype=ep:metrics` (Splunk Edge Processor's self-telemetry). Pipeline-health fields: `pipeline_id`, `events_in`, `events_out`, `dropped_events`, `parse_errors`, `routing_decisions`. ISE-side context from `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog` to confirm receipt. Collected via Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: `Splunk Edge Processor` (Splunk Cloud / Splunk Enterprise 9.x+). — Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352)
spl:
index=_internal sourcetype="ep:metrics" earliest=-30m
| stats sum(events_in) as in, sum(events_out) as out, sum(dropped_events) as drops, sum(parse_errors) as parse_errors by pipeline_id
| eval drop_pct = round((drops/in)*100, 2)
| where drop_pct > 1 OR parse_errors > 0
description: Detects Splunk Edge Processor / Ingest Processor pipeline issues that affect ISE log ingestion — drops, parse errors, routing failures.
value: When Edge Processor is in the path between ISE and Splunk indexers, pipeline health is the missing link in observability. A 5% drop rate is invisible from the Splunk indexer side but obvious from EP metrics.
implementation: Confirm Edge Processor is sending self-telemetry to Splunk. Schedule every 15 min, search window `-30m@m to @m`.
visualization: (1) Per-pipeline drop-rate timechart. (2) Top-N parse errors. (3) Routing-decision distribution.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Planned network maintenance** — Switch/firewall change generates expected deviations for 'Cisco ISE Logs through Splunk Edge Processor — Pipeline Health and Routing'. Cross-check CMDB change records.

2. **New site onboarding** — Baseline metrics unstable first 72h on `_internal`.

3. **Synthetic path monitoring** — Nagios/DNA Center probes from `monitoring_hosts.csv`.

4. **Misconfigured ACL or VLAN** — Single `nas_ip` or segment dominates `ep:metrics` failures.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` with entity, reason, valid_until.
mitreAttack: N/A (ingest pipeline health — measures Splunk Edge Processor for ISE, no adversary technique)
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Edge Processor or Ingest Processor deployed in path.
• Self-telemetry enabled.

Step 1 — Verify telemetry feed.
Step 2 — Search.
Step 3 — Provoke as above.
Step 4 — Dashboard with drop-rate per pipeline.
Step 5 — Troubleshooting: tune pipeline regex; verify EP capacity.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Edge Processor` (Splunk Cloud / Splunk Enterprise 9.x+). — Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=ep:metrics into _internal. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`drop_pct, parse_errors, pipeline_id`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: ISE sends information to Splunk through a middleman. We watch the middleman to make sure it isn't dropping or breaking messages on the way through.
